title: Tessera semantics case
description: One semantics case for the reference interpreter (spec §5): seeded initial state, an ordered sequence of rule calls with their logged external inputs, the tagged result of each call, the expected final state and the expected ordered outputs. Provisional: the AST schema, Core IR schema and diagnostics JSON are not frozen yet (spec §13 freeze order), so this schema is a working contract and pre-freeze rework is accepted. See semantics-case.contract.md.

module.description: Name of the module the case runs against. A case is scoped to one module; names are labels, not identity (spec §1, P7).

initial_state.description: The seeded persistent state the case starts from. Every declared `state` table is seeded here; a table absent from `tables` starts empty.

calls.description: The rule calls to execute, in order. Array order IS the execution order (spec §5.5: serial commits in the order recorded in the input log). Each call's `index` MUST equal its position in this array.

expected_state.description: The persistent state after the last call. On an aborted call the state is unchanged (spec §5.1), so expected_state equals initial_state for the failed tail of a case.

expected_outputs.description: The output elements delivered to the surface, in delivery order: statement source order within a call, then the serial commit order across calls (spec §5, Output). Elements buffered by an aborted call are discarded and MUST NOT appear here.

failureName.description: The name of a failure. `LawViolation`, `DivisionByZero` and `RefinementViolation` are reserved by the spec (§5.2) and MUST NOT be used as user-defined failure names; a case MAY still observe them, because they are what the runtime returns.

state.description: The persistent state: the rows of each declared `state` table. Tables are named; a table with no rows is written as an empty array.

row.description: One row of a `state` table. Field values are the closed literals of spec §2–§3, so a row is JSON-representable and replays identically.

value.description: A closed, deterministic value. `Int` is a JSON integer, `Decimal` a JSON number, `Bool` a JSON boolean, `Text` a JSON string, `Date`/`Duration`/`Instant` an RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 string, an id literal an object tagged `id`, and a record or list a JSON object or array. There is no `null` value: a missing value is absent, never null.

recordValue.description: A record value: the structured element a declared output stream carries (`Stream<Entry>`). Its fields are named values, as in a state row.

idValue.description: An id literal (`#12`, with its declared type ascription) as a tagged object, so an id is distinguishable from a plain `Text`.

typeName.description: The declared type of an id literal: a type name, optionally with one type argument (`Id<Task>`), as the spec writes it (§3).

call.description: One rule call. Its result is exactly one of `Ok(v)` or `Failed(Name)`; a call with neither or with both is invalid.

index.description: Position of this call in the case's `calls` array, counted from 0. The array order and these indices MUST agree.

args.description: The call arguments, in source order.

inputs.description: The external inputs this call consumed, in the order they were logged and consumed. Every clock reading, random draw, id generation and external request is an input (spec §5.6); the log is appended before use, so an input consumed by an aborted call is still logged here.

result.description: The call outcome: `Ok` with the published success value, or `Failed` with the named failure. Exactly one tag is present.

ok.description: The success value published by the call. A rule that returns nothing publishes the unit value.

failed.description: The named failure. The call aborted: no writes, no outputs, no success value (spec §5.1).

kind.description: The kind of external input. `clock` is a clock reading, `random` a random draw, `id` an id generation, `request` an external request.

capability.description: The capability binding the input came from, when the spec gives it a binding name (`clock`, `rng`, `idgen`). Omitted for inputs that are not capability reads.

reading.description: For a `clock` input, which reading it is: `now` (an Instant) or `today` (the UTC calendar Date).

value.description: The logged value of the input. Replaying the log reproduces the run exactly (spec §5.6).

output.description: One delivered output element: the value appended to a declared output stream.

stream.description: The name of the declared output stream the element was appended to.
